glitu · demo
01

Publishing

One markdown file, four outputs

glitu · demo

From one slides.md

  • A standalone page: engine, theme and fonts inside, no network
  • A light page: the engine and the theme come from the web
  • A static site, for any web server
  • An export: editable PowerPoint, vector PDF, PNG images
terminal
glitu build -o talk.html
glitu build --assets https://glitu.net/static
glitu export --format site -o dist
glitu export -o talk.pptx
glitu build -o talk.html
glitu build --assets https://glitu.net/static
glitu export --format site -o dist
glitu export -o talk.pptx
glitu build -o talk.html
glitu build --assets https://glitu.net/static
glitu export --format site -o dist
glitu export -o talk.pptx
glitu build -o talk.html
glitu build --assets https://glitu.net/static
glitu export --format site -o dist
glitu export -o talk.pptx

Everything starts from the same markdown file. One page to carry around, which opens with a double click. A light page that loads the engine from glitu.net. A static site, like Hugo. Or an export, for those who need a file.

glitu · demo
02

History

From the desktop to the browser

glitu · demo

PowerPoint opens the story. Beamer turns slides into source code. Keynote. reveal.js brings them to the browser. Slidev writes them in markdown. glitu keeps the markdown and drops npm.

glitu · demo
03

Architecture

Three crates, one diagram engine

glitu · demo

The markdown goes through glitu; the engine runs it in the browser

Your presentation is plain files. The glitu tool reads them. Its compiler, glitu-core, draws the diagrams with the skemo engine, from its own repository. glitu-web, compiled to WebAssembly, presents them. What you get. And static.glitu.net hosts each version of the engine and of the themes.

In LaTeX, rendered at build

glitu · demo

Energy

  • The equivalence E=mc2E = mc^2
  • A sum ∑i=1ni=n(n+1)2\sum_{i=1}^{n} i = \frac{n(n+1)}{2}
∫−∞+∞e−x2dx=π\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} e^{-x^2}\,dx = \sqrt{\pi}

Start with energy. Then Gauss's sum. Finally the integral.

total.rs
fn total(v: &Vec<i32>) -> i32 {
    let mut s = 0;
    for x in v {
        s += x;
    }
    s
}fn total(v: &[i32]) -> i32 {
    let mut s = 0;
    for x in v {
        s += x;
    }
    s
}fn total(v: &[i32]) -> i32 {
    v.iter().sum()
}

One version per click: the words kept slide to their new place.
